In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the local chemical environment of the alloy is not only a function of the average composition, but also a function of temperature.
the alloy (GaN)(1−x)(ZnO)x has a very high degree of disorder, which is reflected in a large entropy and in the large bond-length fluctuations.
the local chemical environments are strongly affected by the atomic relaxations, and that these in turn have a significant impact on the bond length distribution and on the SRO parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SRO and entropy are found to be very sensitive to the local environments and bond lengths, and that the latter are found to vary significantly with composition and temperature.
the alloy (GaN1−x(Zno)x) is an excellent model system for studying the relation between SRO and entropy in semiconductor alloys.
the alloy system (GaN)0.5(ZnO)0.5 is a good example of a system in which the local atomic environments are strongly correlated with the local composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the entropy of (GaN) 1−x(ZnxO)1−x is dominated by SRO effects, and the SRO parameters and bond lengths can be accurately calculated by combining density functional theory with a cluster expansion.
the local chemical environment of a Ga atom has a strong influence on the local bond-length distribution of Ga atoms, and that this is reflected in the entropy of the alloy.
the bond-length distribution is strongly influenced by the short-range chemical order in (GaN)0.5(ZnO)0.5, which is a direct consequence of the large lattice mismatch between GaN and ZnO.
